title: LSTM
description: Recurrent neural network cell utilizing gate structures to resolve vanishing gradients.
name: LSTM
summary: LSTMs (Long Short-Term Memory) are recurrent neural networks designed to process sequential data, utilizing input, forget, and output gate structures to control gradient flows and capture long-range temporal dependencies.
use_when: Processing real-time streaming sequence data or small-scale low-latency time series.
avoid_when: Working with long document contexts where Transformer models can be trained in parallel.
pros: Mitigates the vanishing gradient problem in RNNs.
Maintains constant memory footprint regardless of sequence length.
cons: Sequential training step restricts utilization of parallel computing.
Prone to forgetting historical context over very long sequences (1000+ steps).
Requires careful initialization of gate biases to prevent saturation.

key_hyperparams.name: hidden_size
key_hyperparams.note: Number of features in the LSTM hidden state. Larger values capture more complexity.

quick_start:
import torch.nn as nn
import torch

model = nn.LSTM(input_size=10, hidden_size=20, num_layers=2)
x = torch.rand((5, 3, 10))
out, (h, c) = model(x)
